```{r}

# Cleaning Pre-Wind Data

clean_wind_panel <- pre_wind %>%
  
# Remove any rows where the operational year is missing
filter(!is.na(p_year)) %>%

# Select only the state, year, and capacity columns
select(t_state, p_year, t_cap) %>%
  
# Group by state and year, and convert individual turbine kW to total MW added
group_by(t_state, p_year) %>%
summarize(mw_added = sum(t_cap, na.rm = TRUE) / 1000, .groups = 'drop') %>%

# Open 50-state grid for pre-trends window
complete(t_state, p_year = 2000:2026, fill = list(mw_added = 0)) %>%
arrange(t_state, p_year) %>%
group_by(t_state) %>%

# Cumulative sum holds capacity at 0 until first project, 
# then holds total capacity flat forward through the years
mutate(total_wind_mw = cumsum(mw_added)) %>%
rename(state = t_state, year = p_year) %>%

# Filter the outcome variable to strictly include 2010-2012
filter(year >= 2010 & year <= 2013)

# Split by each year and pivot year column to display state and capacity by year
clean_wind_panel <- clean_wind_panel %>%
  select(state, year, total_wind_mw) %>%
  group_by(year) %>%
  group_split(.keep = FALSE)
wind_2010 <- clean_wind_panel[[1]]
wind_2011 <- clean_wind_panel[[2]]
wind_2012 <- clean_wind_panel[[3]]

# Used to compare discrepancies between two different data sources for wind capacity
wind_2013_test <- clean_wind_panel[[4]]

```


```{r}

# Cleaning Pre-Solar Data

# 2. Extract state, and 2010 - 2013 capacity data
solar_wide_cumulative <- pre_solar %>%
  select(
    State = 1, 
    raw_2010 = 2, 
    raw_2011 = 3, 
    raw_2012 = 4, 
    raw_2013 = 5
  )

# Convert from solar capacity added to cumulative capacity
solar_wide_cumulative <- solar_wide_cumulative %>%
  mutate(
    # 2010 is just the base year
    Year_2010 = replace_na(raw_2010, 0),
    
    # 2011 = 2010 + 2011
    Year_2011 = 
      replace_na(raw_2010, 0) + 
      replace_na(raw_2011, 0),
    
    # 2012 = 2010 + 2011 + 2012
    Year_2012 = 
      replace_na(raw_2010, 0) + 
      replace_na(raw_2011, 0) + 
      replace_na(raw_2012, 0),
    
    # 2013 = 2010 + 2011 + 2012 + 2013
    # Used to compare discrepancies between two different data sources for solar capacity
    Year_2013_test = 
      replace_na(raw_2010, 0) + 
      replace_na(raw_2011, 0) + 
      replace_na(raw_2012, 0) + 
      replace_na(raw_2013, 0)
  ) %>%
  
  # 5. Output clean state name and cumulative columns for each year
  select(State, Year_2010, Year_2011, Year_2012, Year_2013_test)

```


```{r}

# Cleaning Post-Wind Data

# Add year columns
wind_2010 <- wind_2010 %>%
  rename(State = `state`, wind_capacity = `total_wind_mw`) %>%
  mutate(year = 2010) %>%
  arrange(State)

wind_2011 <- wind_2011 %>%
  rename(State = `state`, wind_capacity = `total_wind_mw`) %>%
  mutate(year = 2011) %>%
  arrange(State)

wind_2012 <- wind_2012 %>%
  rename(State = `state`, wind_capacity = `total_wind_mw`) %>%
  mutate(year = 2012) %>%
  arrange(State)
  
# Loop through every year from 2013 to 2024
for (y in 2013:2024) {
  
  # Generate the variable name ("wind_year")
  var_name <- paste0("wind_", y)
  
  # Temporary data frame to do cleaning
  temp_df <- get(var_name)
  cleaned_df <- temp_df %>%
    
    # Adds the current loop's year
    mutate(year = y) %>%
    rename(wind_capacity = `Nameplate Capacity (MW)`) %>% 
    group_by(State, year) %>% 
    summarize(
      wind_capacity = sum(wind_capacity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
    arrange(State)
  
  # 4. Save the cleaned data frame back to its original variable name
  assign(var_name, cleaned_df)
}

# Combine all years (2010 - 2024)
post_wind_all = bind_rows(
  wind_2010, wind_2011, wind_2012, wind_2013, wind_2014, 
  wind_2015, wind_2016, wind_2017, wind_2018, wind_2019, 
  wind_2020, wind_2021, wind_2022, wind_2023, wind_2024
  )

# To account for discrepancies between pre and post data sources
# Scale pre-trend data
wind_2013_uswtdb <- wind_2013_test %>% 
  rename(State = state, wind_uswtdb = total_wind_mw)

wind_ratios <- wind_2013 %>%
  rename(wind_eia = wind_capacity) %>%
  left_join(wind_2013_uswtdb, by = "State") %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Ratio = EIA Capacity / USWTDB Capacity
    scale_factor = wind_eia / wind_uswtdb
  ) %>%
  mutate(scale_factor = if_else(
    is.nan(scale_factor) | is.infinite(scale_factor), 1, scale_factor)
    ) %>%
  select(State, scale_factor)

# Scale down 2010-2012 wind capacities to meet the EIA baseline
post_wind_all <- post_wind_all %>%
  left_join(wind_ratios, by = "State") %>%
  mutate(
    wind_capacity = if_else(
      year <= 2012, wind_capacity * scale_factor, wind_capacity
      )
  ) %>%
  select(-scale_factor)

# Create a master data frame containing all 48 contiguous states
# Excludes Hawaii and Alaska
contiguous_48 <- state.abb[!state.abb %in% c("AK", "HI")]
master_states <- data.frame(State = contiguous_48)

# Pivot wind data from long format to wide format
wind_wide <- post_wind_all %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year, 
    values_from = wind_capacity,
    names_prefix = "yr_"
  )

# Left join the master list with wind data and sort states alphabetically
final_wind_panel <- master_states %>%
  left_join(wind_wide, by = "State") %>%
  arrange(State)

final_wind_panel_clean <- final_wind_panel %>%
  
  # Temporarily bring columns back to a long format to work row-by-row per state
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("yr_"), 
    names_to = "year", 
    values_to = "wind_capacity"
  ) %>%
  # 2. Group by State and sort by year to ensure sequential order
  group_by(State) %>%
  arrange(State, year) %>%
  # Fill NA values with the previous year's value
  fill(wind_capacity, .direction = "down") %>%
  # If it's still NA (meaning it never had any capacity), replace with 0
  mutate(wind_capacity = replace_na(wind_capacity, 0)) %>%
  # Bring it back to the wide layout
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year, 
    values_from = wind_capacity
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

```


```{r}

# Cleaning Post-Solar Data

# Add year columns
solar_2010 <- solar_wide_cumulative %>%
  select(State, solar_capacity = Year_2010) %>%
  mutate(
    year = 2010,
    State = state.abb[match(State, state.name)]
    ) %>%
  arrange(State)

solar_2011 <- solar_wide_cumulative %>%
  select(State, solar_capacity = Year_2011) %>%
  mutate(
    year = 2011,
    State = state.abb[match(State, state.name)]) %>%
  arrange(State)

solar_2012 <- solar_wide_cumulative %>%
  select(State, solar_capacity = Year_2012) %>%
  mutate(
    year = 2012,
    State = state.abb[match(State, state.name)]) %>%
  arrange(State)

solar_2013_test <- solar_wide_cumulative %>%
  select(State, solar_capacity = Year_2013_test) %>%
  mutate(
    year = 2013,
    State = state.abb[match(State, state.name)]) %>%
  arrange(State)

# Loop through every year from 2013 to 2024
# Same way we did for the post wind data
for (y in 2013:2024) {
  var_name <- paste0("solar_", y)
  temp_df <- get(var_name)
  cleaned_df <- temp_df %>%
    mutate(year = y) %>%
    rename(solar_capacity = `Nameplate Capacity (MW)`) %>% 
    group_by(State, year) %>% 
    summarize(
      solar_capacity = sum(solar_capacity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop"
      ) %>%
    arrange(State)
  assign(var_name, cleaned_df)
}

post_solar_all = bind_rows(
  solar_2010, solar_2011, solar_2012, solar_2013, 
  solar_2014, solar_2015, solar_2016, solar_2017, 
  solar_2018, solar_2019, solar_2020, solar_2021, 
  solar_2022, solar_2023, solar_2024
  )

# Isolate the 2013 Berkeley Lab data and convert names to abbreviations
solar_2013_lbnl_check <- solar_wide_cumulative %>%
  select(State, solar_lbnl = Year_2013_test) %>%
  mutate(
    State = state.abb[match(State, state.name)]
  )

# Join the EIA 2013 data with the Berkeley Lab data
solar_ratios <- solar_2013 %>%
  rename(solar_eia = solar_capacity) %>%
  left_join(solar_2013_lbnl_check, by = "State") %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Create a conditional scale factor to prevent division by zero or Na errors
    # If there's missing or 0 data, don't scale by ratio to avoid dividing by 0
    # Otherwise, scale by the ratio of the two data source values
    scale_factor = if_else(
      is.na(solar_eia) | is.na(solar_lbnl) | solar_eia == 0 | solar_lbnl == 0,
      1,
      solar_eia / solar_lbnl
    )
  ) %>%
  select(State, scale_factor)

# Apply the ratio to the pre-trends years (2010-2012)
post_solar_all <- post_solar_all %>%
  left_join(solar_ratios, by = "State") %>%
  mutate(
    # Double check protection for any lingering NAs
    scale_factor = replace_na(scale_factor, 1),
    solar_capacity = if_else(
      year <= 2012, solar_capacity * scale_factor, solar_capacity
      )
  ) %>%
  select(-scale_factor)

contiguous_48 <- state.abb[!state.abb %in% c("AK", "HI")]
master_states <- data.frame(State = contiguous_48)
solar_wide <- post_solar_all %>%
  group_by(State, year) %>%
  summarize(solar_capacity = sum(solar_capacity, na.rm = TRUE), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year, 
    values_from = solar_capacity,
    names_prefix = "yr_"
  )

final_solar_panel <- master_states %>%
  left_join(solar_wide, by = "State") %>%
  arrange(State)

# Interpolate missing values
final_solar_panel_clean <- final_solar_panel %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("yr_"), 
    names_to = "year", 
    values_to = "solar_capacity"
  ) %>%
  group_by(State) %>%
  arrange(State, year) %>%
  fill(solar_capacity, .direction = "down") %>%
  mutate(solar_capacity = replace_na(solar_capacity, 0)) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = year, 
    values_from = solar_capacity
  ) %>%
  ungroup()

```


```{r}

# Merge state population data: 2010-2019 (Intercensal) 
# + 2020-2024 (Vintage 2024)

# Rename columns: first column is geography, next is 2010 base, then 2011-2019, 
# then 2020 census
colnames(intercensal_raw) <- c(
  "Geography", "Base2010", paste0("Y", 2010:2019), "Census2020"
)

intercensal_states <- intercensal_raw %>%
  filter(grepl("^\\.", Geography)) %>%
  mutate(State = sub("^\\.", "", Geography)) %>%
  filter(State != "Puerto Rico") %>%
  
  # filter(State != "District of Columbia") %>%
  select(State, paste0("Y", 2010:2019)) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = paste0("Y", 2010:2019),
    names_to = "Year",
    values_to = "Population"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(sub("Y", "", Year)))


vintage2024_states <- vintage2024_raw %>%
  filter(trimws(as.character(SUMLEV)) %in% c("40", "040")) %>%
  filter(NAME != "Puerto Rico") %>%
  select(NAME, POPESTIMATE2020, POPESTIMATE2021, POPESTIMATE2022,
                POPESTIMATE2023, POPESTIMATE2024) %>%
  rename(State = NAME) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with("POPESTIMATE"),
    names_to = "Year",
    values_to = "Population"
  ) %>%
  mutate(Year = as.integer(sub("POPESTIMATE", "", Year)))

# Merge into one long-format table: 2010-2024, states only 
state_population_2010_2024 <- dplyr::bind_rows(
  intercensal_states, vintage2024_states
  ) %>%
  arrange(State, Year)

# Reshape to wide format: one row per state, one column per year 
state_population_wide <- state_population_2010_2024 %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = Year, values_from = Population, names_prefix = "Y"
    )

# Map full state names to 2-letter postal codes
population_long <- state_population_2010_2024 %>%
  filter(State %in% c(state.name, "District of Columbia")) %>%
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(Year),
    Population = as.numeric(Population),
    State = case_when(
      State == "District of Columbia" ~ "DC",
      TRUE ~ state.abb[match(State, state.name)]
    )
  ) %>%
  select(State, year, Population)

# Save outputs
write.csv(
  state_population_2010_2024, 
  "state_population_2010_2024_long.csv", 
  row.names = FALSE
  )

write.csv(
  state_population_wide, 
  "state_population_2010_2024_wide.csv", 
  row.names = FALSE
  )

```


```{r}

# Cleaning Real GDP data

gdp_long <- gdp_raw %>%
  # Keep only the Real GDP rows (LineCode is 1)
  filter(LineCode == 1) %>%
  
  # Drop the "United States" row and any regional summaries
  filter(GeoName %in% c(state.name, "District of Columbia")) %>%
  
  # 4. Keep only the State name column and years 2010 - 2024
  select(State = GeoName, `2010`:`2024`) %>%
  
  # Reshape from wide (columns) to long (rows) to match population data
  pivot_longer(
    cols = `2010`:`2024`,
    names_to = "year",
    values_to = "real_gdp"
  ) %>%
  
  # Fix data types, scale by 1 million, 
  # and convert full state names to 2-letter postal codes
  mutate(
    year = as.numeric(year),
    real_gdp = as.numeric(real_gdp) * 1000000, 
    State = case_when(
      State == "District of Columbia" ~ "DC",
      TRUE ~ state.abb[match(State, state.name)]
    )
  )

```


```{r}

# Building the Panel data set

# Create a dedicated long-format version for regressions and plotting
final_wind_panel_long <- final_wind_panel %>%
  
# Remove any rows where the operational year is missing/blank
# Pivot to long format
 pivot_longer(
   cols = starts_with("yr_"), 
   names_to = "year", 
   values_to = "wind_capacity"
 ) %>%
  
# Strip "yr_" so the year column becomes a clean, parse-able number
 mutate(year = as.numeric(gsub("yr_", "", year))) %>%
  
# Sort sequentially by state and year to prepare for the carry-forward step
 group_by(State) %>%
 arrange(State, year) %>%
  
# Handle missing data gaps using Last Observation Carried Forward (LOCF)
 fill(wind_capacity, .direction = "down") %>%
  
# Switch any remaining early NAs to 0
 mutate(wind_capacity = replace_na(wind_capacity, 0)) %>%
  
# Ungroup so it behaves like a standard data frame
 ungroup()

# Create a dedicated long-format version for solar regressions and plotting
final_solar_panel_long <- final_solar_panel %>%
 pivot_longer(
   cols = starts_with("yr_"), 
   names_to = "year", 
   values_to = "solar_capacity"
 ) %>%
 mutate(year = as.numeric(gsub("yr_", "", year))) %>%
 group_by(State) %>%
 arrange(State, year) %>%
 fill(solar_capacity, .direction = "down") %>%
 mutate(solar_capacity = replace_na(solar_capacity, 0)) %>%
 ungroup()

# One-hot-encoding of corporate & municipal issuance, and RPS issuance
# Corporate: 1 if current year >= corporate year, otherwise 0
# Municipal: 1 if current year >= municipal year, otherwise 0
# RPS: 1 if current year >= RPS enacted AND current year < RPS expired
# If never expired, remains 1
# GB: 1 if a state issued either type of green bond, 
# 0 if a state issued neither
policy_clean <- GBI %>%

# 1. Standardize state names to postal abbreviations
 mutate(State = state.abb[match(State, state.name)]) %>%
 filter(!is.na(State)) %>%
  
# 2. Convert character strings/NA values to proper numeric years or infinity
 mutate(
   corp_start = as.numeric(gsub("N/A", NA, `Corporate Year`)),
   muni_start = as.numeric(gsub("N/A", NA, `Municipal Year`)),
   rps_start = as.numeric(gsub("N/A", NA, `RPS Year`)),
   rps_end = as.numeric(gsub("N/A", NA, `RPS Repealed/Expired`)),
    
   # If RPS was never repealed, set its expiration to infinity
   rps_end = if_else(is.na(rps_end), Inf, rps_end)
 ) %>%
 select(State, corp_start, muni_start, rps_start, rps_end)

# Merge Wind and Solar long panels into a single joint panel
joint_energy_panel <- final_wind_panel_long %>%
 full_join(final_solar_panel_long, by = c("State", "year"))

# Combine panels and compute the logical thresholds
final_joint_regression_panel <- final_wind_panel_long %>%

# Join wind and solar together side-by-side
 full_join(final_solar_panel_long, by = c("State", "year")) %>%
  
# Join cleaned timeline parameters
 left_join(policy_clean, by = "State") %>%

# Join population metrics sequentially
 left_join(population_long, by = c("State", "year")) %>%

# Join BEA real GDP metrics sequentially
 left_join(gdp_long, by = c("State", "year")) %>%
  
# Build the binary metrics dynamically
 mutate(
   is_corporate = if_else(!is.na(corp_start) & year >= corp_start, 1, 0),
   is_public = if_else(!is.na(muni_start) & year >= muni_start, 1, 0),
   gb = if_else(is_corporate == 1 | is_public == 1, 1, 0),
    
   # RPS Policy Dummy
   is_rps = if_else(!is.na(rps_start) & year >= rps_start & year < rps_end, 1, 0)
 ) %>%

# Calculate all per capita and economic density metrics
 mutate(
   real_gdp_per_capita       = real_gdp / Population,
   wind_capacity_per_capita  = wind_capacity / Population,
   solar_capacity_per_capita = solar_capacity / Population
 ) %>%
  
# Drop the following columns to only include the one-hot-encodings in the panel
 select(-corp_start, -muni_start, -rps_start, -rps_end)

# Export final panel data set to a CSV file
# This is the data set to be used in Stata for our econometric analysis
write.csv(final_joint_regression_panel, "panel.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```


```{r}

# Improved Treatment: Technology-Specific Green Bond Financing

# Use-of-proceeds audit of the appendix (Table 6): one row per issuer,
# with what the proceeds funded and where the projects are located
gb_uop <- read_csv("green_bond_use_of_proceeds.csv", show_col_types = FALSE) %>%
  mutate(state = state.abb[match(state, state.name)])

# 1. Issuances whose proceeds funded solar and/or wind generation
tech_rows <- gb_uop %>%
  filter(proceeds_to %in% c("Solar", "Wind", "Both")) %>%
  mutate(tech = if_else(proceeds_to == "Both", "solar,wind", tolower(proceeds_to))) %>%
  separate_rows(tech, sep = ",") %>%
  select(state, tech, bond_year = year_table, entity) %>%
  
  # 2. Coding decisions (documented in the CSV's project_location and flag columns)
  # Drop bonds with no in-state capacity: Alabama Power bought out-of-state wind,
  # Forbright lends nationwide
  filter(!entity %in% c("Alabama Power (Southern Co.)", "Forbright Bank")) %>%
  mutate(
    
    # Code by project location, not issuer state
    # TEP (AZ issuer) funded Oso Grande wind in New Mexico
    # SPS (NM issuer) funded Hale wind in Texas
    state = case_when(
      entity == "Tucson Electric Power Co."       ~ "NM",
      entity == "Southwestern Public Service Co." ~ "TX",
      TRUE ~ state
    ),
    
    # One consistent first year for the multistate NSP-Minnesota issuer
    bond_year = if_else(state %in% c("MN", "ND", "SD") & tech == "wind",
                        as.numeric(params$nsp_first_year), as.numeric(bond_year)),
    
    # Medium-confidence codings (project-level allocation not confirmed)
    medium = (state %in% c("OK", "ND", "SD") & tech == "wind") |
             (state == "MS" & tech == "solar")
  ) %>%
  
  # Multistate solar portfolios also treat these states:
  # Duke Energy Carolinas (NC and SC), Dominion Energy (VA, NC, SC and CA)
  bind_rows(tribble(
    ~state, ~tech,   ~bond_year, ~entity,                 ~medium,
    "SC",   "solar", 2018,       "Duke Energy Carolinas", FALSE,
    "NC",   "solar", 2018,       "Dominion Energy",       FALSE,
    "SC",   "solar", 2018,       "Dominion Energy",       FALSE,
    "CA",   "solar", 2018,       "Dominion Energy",       TRUE
  ))

# Robustness option: drop medium-confidence codings
if (!params$include_medium) {
  tech_rows <- tech_rows %>% filter(!medium)
}

# 3. Placebo: verified or issuer-type "Other" bonds (no solar or wind),
# excluding O-I (not an Illinois issuance) and NRG (not a green bond)
other_rows <- gb_uop %>%
  filter(proceeds_to %in% c("Other", "Other (hydro)"),
         confidence != "Not verified",
         !entity %in% c("Owens-Illinois Inc.", "NRG Energy / Texas Issuers")) %>%
  mutate(
    # Brookfield's White Pine hydro bond was issued in 2017, not 2019
    bond_year = if_else(entity == "Brookfield Renewable Partners", 2017, as.numeric(year_table)),
    tech = "other"
  ) %>%
  select(state, tech, bond_year)

# First treatment year by state and technology (0 = never treated)
tech_cohorts <- bind_rows(tech_rows, other_rows) %>%
  group_by(State = state, tech) %>%
  summarize(g = min(bond_year), .groups = "drop") %>%
  pivot_wider(names_from = tech, values_from = g, names_prefix = "g_")

# Corrected baseline: original market-entry coding with documented errors fixed
# IL corporate: O-I's 2019 bond was a euro issue by a Dutch subsidiary; O-I is HQ'd in Ohio
# TX corporate: NRG's 2020 deal was a sustainability-linked bond, not a green bond
# MN, ND, SD corporate: same NSP-Minnesota issuer, so one consistent first year
policy_fix <- policy_clean %>%
  mutate(
    corp_start = case_when(
      State %in% c("IL", "TX") ~ NA_real_,
      State %in% c("MN", "ND", "SD") ~ as.numeric(params$nsp_first_year),
      TRUE ~ corp_start
    )
  ) %>%
  select(State, corp_fix = corp_start, muni_fix = muni_start)

panel_improved <- final_joint_regression_panel %>%
  left_join(tech_cohorts, by = "State") %>%
  left_join(policy_fix, by = "State") %>%
  mutate(

    # Technology-specific cohorts and absorbing treatment dummies
    across(c(g_solar, g_wind, g_other), ~ coalesce(as.numeric(.x), 0)),
    gb_solar = if_else(g_solar > 0 & year >= g_solar, 1, 0),
    gb_wind  = if_else(g_wind  > 0 & year >= g_wind,  1, 0),

    # Placebo: green bonds that funded only non-solar, non-wind uses
    gb_other = if_else(g_other > 0 & year >= g_other, 1, 0),
    placebo_sample = if_else(g_solar == 0 & g_wind == 0, 1, 0),

    # Corrected baseline dummies
    is_corporate_fix = if_else(!is.na(corp_fix) & year >= corp_fix, 1, 0),
    is_public_fix    = if_else(!is.na(muni_fix) & year >= muni_fix, 1, 0),
    gb_fix           = if_else(is_corporate_fix == 1 | is_public_fix == 1, 1, 0),
    g_gb_fix         = coalesce(pmin(corp_fix, muni_fix, na.rm = TRUE), 0),
    g_corp_fix       = coalesce(corp_fix, 0),
    g_muni_fix       = coalesce(muni_fix, 0),

    # Outcomes in watts per person (Table 1 definition) and log transforms
    solar_w_pc  = solar_capacity_per_capita * params$watts_scale,
    wind_w_pc   = wind_capacity_per_capita  * params$watts_scale,
    ln_solar_pc = log(solar_w_pc + 1),
    ln_wind_pc  = log(wind_w_pc + 1),
    ln_gdp_pc   = log(real_gdp_per_capita),

    # Numeric state identifier for did::att_gt()
    state_id = as.integer(factor(State))
  ) %>%
  select(-corp_fix, -muni_fix) %>%
  arrange(State, year)

```


```{r}

# Checks on panel_improved

# Balanced panel: 48 states x 15 years, one row per state-year
stopifnot(
  nrow(panel_improved) == 48 * 15,
  !any(duplicated(panel_improved[c("State", "year")]))
)

# Every treatment dummy is absorbing (never switches from 1 back to 0)
absorbing <- panel_improved %>%
  group_by(State) %>%
  summarize(across(c(gb_solar, gb_wind, gb_other, gb_fix), ~ all(diff(.x) >= 0)),
            .groups = "drop")
stopifnot(all(absorbing[-1]))

# Cohort sizes under each treatment definition
cohort_table <- function(gvar) {
  panel_improved %>%
    distinct(State, g = .data[[gvar]]) %>%
    count(g, name = "states") %>%
    mutate(g = if_else(g == 0, "Never treated", as.character(g)))
}
knitr::kable(cohort_table("g_wind"),  caption = "Wind treatment cohorts")
knitr::kable(cohort_table("g_solar"), caption = "Solar treatment cohorts")
knitr::kable(cohort_table("g_other"), caption = "Placebo treatment cohorts")

# State-years where the corrected baseline differs from the original gb
panel_improved %>%
  filter(gb != gb_fix | is_corporate != is_corporate_fix) %>%
  count(State, name = "state_years_changed") %>%
  knitr::kable(caption = "Changes from original to corrected baseline coding")

# Export improved panel for Stata and R
# - Drop the original market-entry dummies (is_corporate, is_public, gb), which
#   contain the coding errors, and keep the corrected versions under the
#   original names so existing Stata code runs unchanged
# - Drop the cohort-year columns (g_*); every treatment variable exported is 0/1
#   (Stata rebuilds first-treatment years with egen, as in JoE_Stata.do)
panel_improved_export <- panel_improved %>%
  select(-is_corporate, -is_public, -gb, -starts_with("g_")) %>%
  rename(is_corporate = is_corporate_fix,
         is_public    = is_public_fix,
         gb           = gb_fix) %>%
  select(State, year, wind_capacity, solar_capacity, Population, real_gdp,
         is_corporate, is_public, gb, gb_wind, gb_solar, gb_other,
         placebo_sample, is_rps, everything())

# Every treatment variable must be strictly 0 or 1
treatment_vars <- c("is_corporate", "is_public", "gb", "gb_wind", "gb_solar",
                    "gb_other", "placebo_sample", "is_rps")
stopifnot(all(sapply(panel_improved_export[treatment_vars],
                     function(x) all(x %in% c(0, 1)))))

write.csv(panel_improved_export, "panel_improved.csv", row.names = FALSE)

```


```{r}

# Plotting helpers shared by all figures

# Line chart of capacity per capita: thin lines for each state,
# thick lines for the average of treated vs never-treated states
plot_capacity_lines <- function(outcome, gvar, tech, file) {

  line_data <- panel_improved %>%
    mutate(group = if_else(.data[[gvar]] > 0,
                           paste(tech, "green bond financing"),
                           paste("Never treated for", tolower(tech)))) %>%
    select(State, year, group, value = all_of(outcome))

  group_means <- line_data %>%
    group_by(year, group) %>%
    summarize(value = mean(value), .groups = "drop")

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_line(data = line_data,
              aes(x = year, y = value, group = State, color = group),
              linewidth = 0.4, alpha = 0.35) +
    geom_line(data = group_means, aes(x = year, y = value, color = group),
              linewidth = 1.4) +
    scale_color_manual(
      values = setNames(c("#C07A5A", "gray55"),
                        c(paste(tech, "green bond financing"),
                          paste("Never treated for", tolower(tech)))),
      name = NULL
    ) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2010, 2024, by = 2)) +
    labs(
      title = paste(tech, "Capacity Per Capita Over Time For Lower 48 States (2010 - 2024)"),
      subtitle = "Thin lines are individual states; thick lines are group means",
      x = "Year",
      y = paste(tech, "Capacity Per Capita (W / Person)")
    ) +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "bottom",
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, color = "gray30")
    )

  print(p)
  ggsave(filename = file, plot = p, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)
}

# Choropleth of 2024 capacity per capita, labeling the treated states
plot_capacity_map <- function(outcome, gvar, tech, file) {

  map_2024 <- panel_improved %>%
    filter(year == 2024) %>%
    select(State, capacity = all_of(outcome)) %>%
    mutate(region = tolower(state.name[match(State, state.abb)]))

  geo_data <- map_data("state") %>%
    left_join(map_2024, by = "region")

  treated_states <- panel_improved %>%
    distinct(State, g = .data[[gvar]]) %>%
    filter(g > 0) %>%
    pull(State)

  treated_labels <- data.frame(
    State = state.abb,
    long = state.center$x,
    lat = state.center$y
  ) %>%
    filter(!State %in% c("AK", "HI"), State %in% treated_states)

  p <- ggplot() +
    geom_polygon(data = geo_data,
                 aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group, fill = capacity),
                 color = "white", linewidth = 0.2) +
    geom_text(data = treated_labels, aes(x = long, y = lat, label = State),
              color = "black", fontface = "bold", size = 3.5, check_overlap = TRUE) +
    scale_fill_gradientn(
      name = "W / Person",
      colors = c("#E6D3B3", "#D49A73", "#C07A5A"),
      labels = scales::comma_format(accuracy = 0.1),
      na.value = "grey90"
    ) +
    coord_map("albers", lat0 = 39, lat1 = 45) +
    labs(
      title = paste("Cumulative US", tech, "Capacity Per Capita by State (2024)"),
      subtitle = paste("Labeled states received green bond financing for in-state",
                       tolower(tech), "capacity")
    ) +
    theme_void() +
    theme(
      legend.position = "right",
      legend.box.margin = margin(t = 0, r = 20, b = 0, l = 0),
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold"),
      plot.subtitle = element_text(hjust = 0.5, size = 10, color = "gray30")
    )

  print(p)
  ggsave(filename = file, plot = p, width = 10, height = 6, dpi = 300)
}

# Stacked timeline of first treatment year, one label per state
plot_timeline <- function(gvar, title, color, file) {

  timeline_data <- panel_improved %>%
    distinct(State, year = .data[[gvar]]) %>%
    filter(year > 0) %>%
    arrange(year, State) %>%
    group_by(year) %>%
    mutate(stack_index = row_number()) %>%
    ungroup()

  p <- ggplot(timeline_data, aes(x = year, y = stack_index, label = State)) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, color = "gray50", linewidth = 0.5) +
    geom_text(color = color, fontface = "bold", size = 4.5) +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(2013, 2024, by = 1), limits = c(2012.5, 2024.5)) +
    scale_y_continuous(expand = expansion(mult = c(0.1, 0.2))) +
    labs(title = title, x = "Year of First Qualifying Issuance", y = "") +
    theme_minimal() +
    theme(
      plot.title = element_text(hjust = 0.5, face = "bold", size = 14),
      panel.grid.major.y = element_blank(),
      panel.grid.minor.y = element_blank(),
      axis.text.y = element_blank(),
      axis.ticks.y = element_blank()
    )

  print(p)
  ggsave(filename = file, plot = p, width = 10, height = 5, dpi = 300)
}
```
